newsitem.title: USA: Liposome stock plunges on test drug failure.
newsitem.headline: Liposome stock plunges on test drug failure.

text.p: Liposome Co. Inc. said Wednesday its test drug to treat acute respiratory distress syndrome failed to perform as expected, sparking a sell-off that wiped out nearly 63 percent of its market value.
Liposome's stock plunged $15.625 to $9.19 on Nasdaq, where it was the biggest loser of the day and the most active issue, with 14.5 million shares changing hands by late morning.
"The stock is getting hammered," a trader said.
Morgan Stanley, which had previously rated the stock outperform, downgraded it to neutral.
Liposome, a biopharmaceutical company based in Princeton, N.J., said the Phase III study of its Ventus drug showed no difference between patients receiving the drug or a placebo.

"We are very disappointed in the results of this study," Chairman Charles Baker said in a statement. "We will continue to evaluate the drug to determine whether it can play a role in the treatment of patients with ARDS (acute respiratory distress syndrome)."
Liposome will also continue to evaluate whether the drug may be useful in other clinical settings, he said.
